thread:
sam: FYI infra repo GH Actions keeps failing on the apply step in ap-southeast1 — terraform hangs when provisioning GPU nodepool. Error in logs looks like "InsufficientIPAddresses" and the runner warmup times out. Anyone seen this pattern?

infra-ci-bot: GH Actions run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/runs/1234567890 — job: apply (failed), step: create_nodepool, exit_code: 1

priya: Saw a similar spike yesterday in canary. GKE CNI reported unable to assign pod IPs; events show "failed to allocate IP from secondary range". Might be secondary IP exhaustion on the subnet.

jordan: Can you paste the apply log snippet or kubectl events? Also which cluster (name) and subnet are we hitting?

sam: cluster: gpu-prod-ap1, subnet: redwood-gpu-subnet-ap1-secondary. Log snippet:

```
Error: googleapi: Error 403: Quota 'IN_USE_ADDRESSES' exceeded. Allowed: 1024 Used: 1024, quotaExceeded
terraform: creating google_container_node_pool.gpu: still creating... (10m elapsed)
Warning  FailedCreatePodSandBox  13m   kubelet  Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to assign IP from range: allocation failed
```

...and GH runner logs show long cache restore times and then runner boot timeout at ~9m.

taylor: We're spinning up a lot of ephemeral GPU clusters for CI smoke tests this week (concurrency 5). Two things: 1) concurrency + bursts are driving up IP usage; 2) cache restore from s3/gcs is slow so runners stay warm longer and hold IPs. Short term: reduce concurrency to 2 for infra workflows and add retry/backoff on nodepool creation.

priya: Agreed. Short term steps I can do: update .github/workflows/apply.yml to set concurrency/group and add a 60s retry loop around terraform apply for 3 attempts. Also we should pin nodepool creation to smaller initial node count and use autoscaling to avoid allocating full pool immediately.

jordan: Also check subnet secondary ranges: run `gcloud compute networks subnets describe redwood-gpu-subnet-ap1 --region=asia-southeast1 --format=\"yaml(secondaryIpRanges)\"` — we may be at the limit. Long term we should expand the secondary range or create a dedicated VPC for GPU pools.

infra-ci-bot: New workflow run queued: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/runs/1234567891 — propose_concurrency-change branch

sam: I pushed a quick change to reduce concurrency and add retries. Also switched the job runner label to gpu-warm (prewarmed pool) to reduce warmup time. Patch applied: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412

taylor: Nice. For immediate mitigation I've temporarily lowered infra repo GH Actions concurrency to 2 (org setting) and disabled parallel smoke runs in the scheduled job.

priya: I'll open a ticket to increase secondary IP allocation for redwood-gpu-subnet-ap1 and add an alert when used > 80% so CI doesn't silently exhaust it next time. Ticket: RD-ENG-8345

sam: After the change, new apply run succeeded on the second attempt. :white_check_mark: We should still treat this as P2 — action items: expand secondary range, add IP usage alert, consider a small pool of long-lived prewarmed GPU runners for infra applies.

jordan: For the rollout automation side, we should also add a fallback: if create_nodepool fails with IP/quota errors, automatically back off and use a smaller node count or a non-gpu fallback pool instead of failing the whole pipeline.

priya: Agreed. I'll draft a short RFC for fallback policies and include cost tradeoffs (prewarmed pool vs slower fallback). Will link here when ready.

sam: Thanks all. Marking thread resolved for now; follow-ups in RD-ENG-8345 and the RFC.
